notable_claims: Academic freedom in the classroom is necessary to prevent a chilling effect on instruction.
Market forces are unlikely to force universities to shut down due to bad policies.
The protection of incompetent faculty is a failure of tenure implementation, not a failure of academic freedom.
classification.summary: Dean Gottehrer argues against the notion that market forces naturally penalize universities with restrictive policies. He defends academic freedom in both research and the classroom as essential to prevent 'academic pablum' and the politicization of education. Gottehrer contends that while tenure can protect incompetents, this is a failure of the awarding process rather than a flaw in the concept of academic freedom.
classification.title: Re: University Marketplace

notable_claims: The EFF hosted an anonymous FTP archive dedicated to Computers and Academic Freedom.
Professor John McCarthy led efforts to restore the 'rec.humor.funny' newsgroup at Stanford after it was suppressed in 1989.
NCSA revised its email policy on April 23, 1991, shortly after a critique claiming it was inconsistent with the Constitution and academic freedom was distributed.
classification.summary: This item is a README file describing the electronic library of information regarding computers and academic freedom hosted by the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF). It lists various archived materials, including mailing list digests, legal documents like the ECPA, and case studies on censorship at Stanford University and NCSA. The archive served as a centralized repository for early digital rights advocacy and academic freedom debates.
classification.title: Contents of comp-academic-freedom archives @ eff.org

notable_claims: Computer security policies must be a joint effort between technical personnel and decision-makers to be implementable and enforceable.
Acceptable use policies should explicitly define whether 'hacking' for security research purposes is permitted and under what controls.
There is a fundamental tradeoff between a user's right to privacy and a system administrator's need to diagnose problems or investigate violations.
classification.summary: Carl Kadie shares excerpts from RFC 1244 ('Site Security Handbook') regarding the creation of computer security policies. The text outlines essential considerations for acceptable use policies, including user rights, administrator privileges, and the ethical implications of 'hacking' for research purposes. It emphasizes that policy creation should be a joint effort between technical personnel and decision-makers.
classification.title: Re: Authority of Public Universities

classification.summary: A brief message sent by Carl M. Kadie regarding censorship. The provided text contains only the header information and no body content.
classification.title: FYI: Censorship

notable_claims: Computing administrators at CMU once threatened to revoke user IDs over perceived obscene job names on punched cards.
classification.summary: Joseph Newcomer recounts an anecdote from his time at Carnegie Mellon University involving a dispute over a job name used on punched cards. The assistant director of computing accused him of using obscene language, which Newcomer countered by claiming the name was a Latin acronym. This highlights early tensions between users and computing administrators regarding acceptable use and censorship.
classification.title: Censorship
